title: Cohomology of punctured generalization neighborhoods as a filtered colimit
statement: Let $T$ be a spectral topological space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $Z\subseteq T$ be closed with quasi-compact open complement $U=T\setminus Z$, and let $A$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $T$. Set $W=\{t\in T:\overline{\{t\}}\cap Z\ne\varnothing\}$ and $S=W\setminus Z$, with their subspace topologies. For a subspace $B\subseteq T$, write $A|_B$ for the inverse image along its inclusion [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. For every integer $p\geq0$ the canonical restriction maps induce an isomorphism of abelian groups $$\varinjlim_{Z\subseteq N\subseteq T,\ N\text{ quasi-compact open}} H^p(N\setminus Z,A|_{N\setminus Z})\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^p(S,A|_S).$$ Here cohomology is the right-derived global sections of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is over the set of quasi-compact open neighborhoods $N$ of $Z$, ordered by reverse inclusion, with restriction transition maps. This index set is nonempty (it contains $T$) and directed (intersections are quasi-compact open).

source.place: Tag 0A3D, label lemma-cohomology-of-neighbourhoods-of-closed, part (2), specialized to a closed subset whose open complement is quasi-compact; such Z is constructible and quasi-compact in a spectral space

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of quasi-compact open neighborhoods of $Z$, with $N\le M$ meaning $M\subseteq N$. It contains $T$ and $N\cap M$ is a common upper bound by the quasi-separated clause of [def-weil-spectral-space]. The closed subset $Z$ is quasi-compact: append the open $T\setminus Z$ to any open cover of $Z$ and use quasi-compactness of $T$. Every $t\in W$ belongs to every such $N$, since an open containing a specialization of $t$ contains $t$. Conversely, if $t\notin W$, the closed set $\overline{\{t\}}$ misses $Z$. Cover $Z$ by quasi-compact basis opens contained in $T\setminus\overline{\{t\}}$ and take a finite subcover. Their union is a quasi-compact open neighborhood of $Z$ missing $t$. Thus $W=\bigcap_{N\in I}N$ and $S=\bigcap_{N\in I}(N\setminus Z)$. For $Z=\varnothing$ the same argument uses the empty union.

source.place: Tag 0A31, label lemma-make-spectral-space, proof (3) implies (4); specialized argument written out

proof.text: Put $X_N=N\setminus Z=N\cap U$. Each $X_N$ is quasi-compact open in $T$, since $N,U$ are quasi-compact open and $T$ is quasi-separated. Any quasi-compact open $V$ of a spectral space is itself spectral: it is quasi-compact; its quasi-compact opens are exactly the quasi-compact ambient opens contained in $V$, so the ambient basis and intersection property restrict to it. For sobriety, if $C$ is a nonempty irreducible closed subset of $V$, its closure in $T$ is irreducible with unique generic point $\eta$; because $V$ meets that closure and is open, it contains $\eta$, and $C=V\cap\overline{\{\eta\}}$. Uniqueness follows from uniqueness in $T$ after taking closure in $T$. This verifies all clauses of [def-weil-spectral-space] for $X_N$. For $M\subseteq N$, the inclusion $X_M\hookrightarrow X_N$ is spectral: a quasi-compact open $B$ of $X_N$ is also a quasi-compact open of $T$, and its inverse image is $B\cap X_M$, quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, quasi-compact-open case; direct proof from spectral-space definition

proof.text: The inclusions $p_N:S\hookrightarrow X_N$ exhibit a topological inverse limit. Indeed compatible points of the $X_N$ are all the same point, since any two indices have a common upper bound; they are therefore exactly the points of $\bigcap_N X_N=S$. The initial topology of these maps is the subspace topology: all maps are continuous for that topology, and the coordinate $N=T$ is the inclusion into $U$, which already induces the subspace topology of $T$ on $S$. The directed set and spectral transition maps were checked in steps 1 and 2, so [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral] implies that $S$ is spectral and the $p_N$ are spectral.

source.place: Tag 0A2Z, label lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces; Tag 0AP0, label lemma-make-spectral-space-minus, intersection-limit argument

proof.text: Take $F_N=A|_{X_N}$. Since $X_N$ is open in $T$, the presheaf inverse image in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] is just restriction (an open of $X_N$ is open in $T$ and is a terminal neighborhood in that colimit), already a sheaf. Thus the maps $F_N\to(f_{NM})_*F_M$ are ordinary restriction maps, whose identity and composition laws hold section by section. On $S$, each $p_N^{-1}F_N$ identifies canonically with $A|_S$. To see both the identification and its compatibility, for composable continuous maps $h,k$ use the adjunction bijections $\mathrm{Hom}(k^{-1}h^{-1}B,C)=\mathrm{Hom}(B,h_*k_*C)=\mathrm{Hom}(B,(hk)_*C)$, since direct images compose sectionwise. The representing isomorphism to $(hk)^{-1}B$ is uniquely determined by sending the composite unit to the unit for $hk$; for three maps both composites send the same unit to the same unit, hence are equal. Explicitly, write $j_N:X_N\hookrightarrow T$ and $c(h,k):k^{-1}h^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(h\circ k)^{-1}$ for these unit-compatible composition isomorphisms. For $N\le M$, the adjoint restriction map is $\beta_{NM}=c(j_N,f_{NM})_A:f_{NM}^{-1}F_N\to F_M$, because on every open it is the identity after restriction. The transition on the pulled-back sheaves is $t_{NM}=p_M^{-1}(\beta_{NM})\circ c(f_{NM},p_M)_{F_N}^{-1}$. Set $\theta_N=c(j_N,p_N)_A:p_N^{-1}F_N\xrightarrow{\sim}A|_S$. Associativity of the unit-compatible composition isomorphisms, proved by the preceding Hom calculation, gives $\theta_M\circ t_{NM}=\theta_N$. Hence all transition maps become identities on $A|_S$. This constant diagram has $A|_S$ as its colimit: compatible maps from its terms to any sheaf are a single map, because $I$ is nonempty and any two indices have a common upper bound. This is exactly the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, preceding setup, for the restriction system; inverse images from Sheaves Section 008C

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-cohomology] to the small directed set $I$, the spectral spaces $X_N$, their spectral inclusions, the spectral limit $S$ and the abelian-sheaf restriction system $F_N$. All hypotheses are verified in steps 1--4. Its sheaf colimit is $A|_S$ by step 4, hence it gives the asserted isomorphism in each degree $p\ge0$. Its comparison leg at $N$ is the pullback along $S\hookrightarrow X_N$ followed by the coefficient-colimit leg. Under the unit-compatible identification of step 4 that coefficient leg is the canonical restriction identification with $A|_S$. Therefore this is precisely the canonical restriction map in the stated conclusion, with the stated restriction transition maps, not merely an abstract isomorphism of groups.
